# git: alias: add rework command for interactive rebase that keeps dates

Add `git rework`, an interactive rebase that keeps dates: `git rebase -i --committer-date-is-author-date "$@"`. **Motivation:** squash, fixup, reorder and edit in `rebase -i` reset the committer date of every replayed commit to now, so the reworked range ends up hours or months "ahead" of its neighbours, and the child-older-than-parent breaks show up in date-based tooling and the contributions calendar. `git amend` ([[DOT-352]]) and `git rewrite` ([[DOT-498]]) already keep dates for the last commit; there is no such path for a range. Since Git 2.29 the flag works with the merge backend, i.e. together with `-i`.

```bash
$ git rework HEAD~3                  # squash/reorder the last three, dates kept
$ git rework --autosquash main       # args are passed through as is
$ git log --format='%h %ad | %cd' --date=iso HEAD~3..   # %ad == %cd on every rewritten commit
```

Decisions to make: plain alias vs `git-rework` function in `bin/lib/git/commit.bash` next to `git-amend`/`git-rewrite` (for consistency, and for a Git version check); how it relates to the fixup alias in [[DOT-343]] (`git fixup` could end with `git rework --autosquash`) and to the squash item of [[DOT-500]]. Out of scope: non-interactive `rebase`/`pull --rebase` in the sync scripts, rewriting published histories.
